The issue is that the `updateSkill` function takes two parameters: `id: number` and `formData: FormData`. However, when you use a server action with a form's `action` attribute, it only receives the `FormData` as a single argument.

In Next.js, there are a few ways to handle this:

1. **Using `.bind()`** - You can bind the first argument (id) to the server action, so when the form submits, it passes the id as the first argument and formData as the second.

2. **Using a hidden input field** - Include the id as a hidden input in the form, and extract it from formData in the server action.

3. **Using closure with an inline function** - But this doesn't work directly with server actions on forms.

The recommended approach in Next.js 14+ (and 15/16) is to use `.bind()` to pass additional arguments to server actions.

Looking at your code, the issue is that your `updateSkill` server action expects two parameters (`id` and `formData`), but when you use it directly in the form's `action` prop, it only receives `FormData`.

In Next.js, the recommended way to pass additional arguments to server actions is using JavaScript's `.bind()` method. Here's how to fix it:

## Solution

**1. Update the page to bind the id to the server action:**

```tsx
import { db } from "@/db";
import { skills } from "@/db/schema/portfolio";
import { updateSkill } from "@/lib/actions/skills";
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";

export default async function UpdateSkillDashboardPage(props: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
    const params = await props.params;
    const id = Number(params.id);

    const skill = await db.select().from(skills).where(eq(skills.id, id));
    const skillResult = skill[0];

    // Bind the id as the first argument
    const updateSkillWithId = updateSkill.bind(null, id);

    return (
        <form action={updateSkillWithId} className="flex flex-col">
            <h1>Edit the skill</h1>
            <div>
                <label htmlFor="name">Name:</label>
                <input type="text" name="name" id="name" placeholder="name" defaultValue={skillResult.name} />
            </div>
            <div>
                <label htmlFor="type">Type:</label>
                <select name="type" id="type" defaultValue={skillResult.type}>
                    <option value="fullstack">Full Stack</option>
                    <option value="frontend">Frontend</option>
                    <option value="backend">Backend</option>
                    <option value="database">Database</option>
                    <option value="devops">DevOps</option>
                    <option value="practices">Practices</option>
                    <option value="tools">Tools</option>
                    <option value="other">Other</option>
                </select>
            </div>
            <div>
                <label htmlFor="icon">Icon:</label>
                <input type="text" name="icon" id="icon" placeholder="icon" defaultValue={skillResult.icon || ""} />
            </div>
            <div>
                <label htmlFor="url">URL:</label>
                <input type="text" name="url" id="url" placeholder="url" defaultValue={skillResult.url || ""} />
            </div>
            <button type="submit">Edit {skillResult.name}!</button>
        </form>
    )
}
```

**Key changes:**
1. Use `updateSkill.bind(null, id)` to create a new function with `id` pre-bound as the first argument
2. Changed `value` to `defaultValue` on inputs — this is important because `value` makes them controlled components which won't work in a Server Component without client-side state
